newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium seen selling more ASLK-CGER bank to Fortis.
newsitem.headline: Belgium seen selling more ASLK-CGER bank to Fortis.

text.p: The Belgian government will announce in its 1997 budget statement next week that it will exercise its put option to sell more of Belgian bank and insurance company ASLK-CGER to the Fortis financial group, Belgian newspapers reported on Wednesday.
Government officials declined to confirm the reports and a spokesman for Belgian-Dutch Fortis in Brussels said the company had not been formally approached about a possible sale.
"At this stage it's very difficult to comment. We are waiting to see what the proposal from the government will be and then we will evaluate it," Fortis spokesman Corneel Maes said.
Under a 1993 agreement by which Fortis acquired an initial 49.9 percent of ASLK-CGER for 34.13 billion Belgian francs, the Belgian government can sell Fortis a further 9.8 percent of the bank.
Fortis also has a first right of refusal on a further 15 percent of ASLK-CGER.

"In the 1993 agreement a price (for the 9.8 percent) was fixed but I would rather not quote a figure. The price is related to a complicated formula based on interest rates and so on, but we have a fairly good idea what it would be," Maes told Reuters.
"Since we purchased ASLK in 1993 we have known this put option could be exercised and so it has been included in the calculations on funding our expansion strategy," Maes added.

Belgian newspapers said on Wednesday the government would next week announce plans to sell in total 24.8 percent of Fortis, including the 9.8 percent it would sell to Fortis using its put option. De Financieel Economische Tijd reported, however, it had not been decided whether to sell the additional 15 percent directly to Fortis or through a bourse listing.
Maes noted that the price of the further 15 percent block was negotiatble despite Fortis's right of refusal.
